Stop averagingthe wind.

A SCADA historian keeps the ten-minute mean. Gale keeps the 30,000 samples behind it: every channel on every turbine, ingested at 4.8 million readings a second per node and queryable at full resolution.

Sheet 2 of 2 — Ingest

The wind is chaotic.
The clocks aren’t.

Every channel on a turbine samples on a fixed clock. Gale stores time as the change in the sampling interval: at a steady 50 Hz that change is zero, and zero costs one bit. The bits go to the values instead — each reading’s difference from the last, in the sensor’s own integer counts, packed to exactly the width it needs. Sixteen bytes become about 1.3, so the write-ahead log, the disk and the network each carry a twelfth of the load.

  1. ARaw — 8 B timestamp + 8 B value = 16 B per reading
  2. BTime — Δ² of a 50 Hz clock is 0 → 1 bit
  3. CValue — zigzag Δ in 0.01 m/s counts → 1 bit, or 5 + width
  4. DSealed — 96 readings: 1,536 B → 127 B. 1.32 B each, 12.1× smaller
